## Explanations

### Warm-up

First a few things from last time: the 1st tone (high, flat) and the 4th tone (falling).

**mā** (mum) · **mà** (to scold)  

### 3rd tone: low

Drop your voice low and keep it relaxed. A bit creaky is fine.

English: a low, doubtful *Hmm…* German: a reluctant *Na ja…*

Said on its own, it often rises a little at the end. Inside a sentence it mostly just stays **low**. Beginners make it too bouncy, so think *low*, not *down-up*.

The mark is a little valley: **ǎ**.

**mǎ** (horse) · **wǒ** · **nǐ** · **hǎo**  

### High, low or falling?

Here are the three tones you know now, on the same syllables. Play each row a few times and draw the shapes in the air with your hand.

**mā** (mum) · **mǎ** (horse) · **mà** (to scold)  
**hāo** · **hǎo** · **hào**  
**nī** · **nǐ** · **nì**  

### Coming soon: nǐ hǎo

You probably know **nǐ hǎo** (hello). It's two 3rd tones in a row, and that makes the first one change. That gets its own lesson, so for now we leave it out.

## New words

| Pinyin | Meaning | Note |
|--------|---------|------|
| **wǒ**<br><sub>wo3</sub> | I, me | Like English woe, but low. I and me are the same word. |
| **nǐ**<br><sub>ni3</sub> | you | Like English knee, but low. |
| **hǎo**<br><sub>hao3</sub> | good; OK | Hǎo! on its own means OK! / Fine! The ao sounds like English how (with a rough German h). |

## New phrases

| Pinyin | English | Literally |
|--------|---------|-----------|
| **Wǒ bù hē.**<br><sub>Wo3 bu4 he1.</sub> | I don't drink. / I won't have any. | I / not / drink |
| **Shì wǒ.**<br><sub>Shi4 wo3.</sub> | It's me. | is / me |
| **Hǎo, wǒ hē.**<br><sub>Hao3, wo3 he1.</sub> | OK, I'll drink (some). | OK / I / drink |
